## 1. Presets and receiver profiles

### 1.1 Sender presets (spec 1.7)

`EncoderConfig::from_preset(preset, 8000)`, every preset on 1500 Hz with 8 sync markers, a 250 ms tune tone and a 100 ms tail. Net rate = N / ((N + 1) T); overhead = lead-in + tune + sync + END + tail. The band is `occupied_band(config)`; the fit and the shift tolerance are `passband_fit(config)` in the preset's own passband: how far the pitch may move down / up and still pass the filter and be found by the receiver that hears it.

| Preset | T | N | Pitch | Slots/s | Net bit/s | Passband | Lead-in | Tune | Overhead | Occupied band | Shift tolerance | −26 dB width | Heard by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hf_slow` | 32 ms | 8 | 1500 Hz | 31.25 | **27.78** | 300–2700 Hz | 0 ms | 8 slots, 256 ms | 676 ms | 138 Hz, 1431–1569 Hz | ±1131 Hz | 219 Hz | ssb, am, fm |
| `hf` | 16 ms | 8 | 1500 Hz | 62.50 | **55.56** | 300–2700 Hz | 0 ms | 16 slots, 256 ms | 516 ms | 276 Hz, 1362–1638 Hz | ±1062 Hz | 438 Hz | ssb, am, fm |
| `hf_fast` | 8 ms | 8 | 1500 Hz | 125.00 | **111.11** | 300–2700 Hz | 0 ms | 32 slots, 256 ms | 436 ms | 550 Hz, 1225–1775 Hz | ±925 Hz | 875 Hz | ssb, am, fm |
| `am` | 8 ms | 16 | 1500 Hz | 125.00 | **117.65** | 100–3000 Hz | 0 ms | 32 slots, 256 ms | 436 ms | 550 Hz, 1225–1775 Hz | −1125 / +1200 Hz | 875 Hz | ssb, am, fm |
| `fm` | 4 ms | 16 | 1500 Hz | 250.00 | **235.29** | 300–3000 Hz | 300 ms | 63 slots, 252 ms | 692 ms | 1100 Hz, 950–2050 Hz | −500 / +950 Hz | 1750 Hz | fm |

"Heard by": the profiles whose window holds T, whose tone search holds the pitch and whose passband holds the occupied band (`DecoderConfig::search_range()`, `passband_fit()`).

## 2. "Hi" = 0x48 0x69, bit by bit (spec 2.2)

The bytes are one stream of bits, most significant bit first: `01001000 01101001`. The stream is cut into packages of N bits; each package is START, its bits, STOP, and each STOP is the START of the next package. The last sync marker is the first START; END is two markers after the last STOP. Timing below: the hf preset (T 16 ms, 1500 Hz) at 8000 Hz, with N changed where stated.

### 2.1 Packages for N = 8, 4 and 3

| N | Packages (START … STOP each) | Data slots + STOPs | Slots in the transmission | `duration_samples(2)` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 (the HF presets: one byte per package) | `01001000` · `01101001` | 18 | 44 | 6432 samples = 804 ms |
| 4 (Gustavo's first picture: two packages per byte) | `0100` · `1000` · `0110` · `1001` | 20 | 46 | 6688 samples = 836 ms |
| 3 (a byte spans packages; a short final package) | `010` · `010` · `000` · `110` · `100` · `1` | 22 | 48 | 6944 samples = 868 ms |

## 3. Packets (spec 2.6)

`packet_build()` wraps a payload as `[2D D4][LEN hi][LEN lo][payload][CRC hi][CRC lo]`; the CRC is CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE (poly 0x1021, init 0xFFFF) over the two LEN bytes and the payload; `crc16_ccitt("123456789")` = 0x29B1.

### 3.1 "CQ DE PY2"

| Field | Bytes |
|---|---|
| sync | `2D D4` |
| LEN (16 bits, big-endian) | `00 09` = 9 |
| payload "CQ DE PY2" | `43 51 20 44 45 20 50 59 32` |
| CRC over LEN + payload | `F4 E5` = 0xF4E5 |

Packet: 15 bytes `2D D4 00 09 43 51 20 44 45 20 50 59 32 F4 E5`.

As packages (the bytes of the packet, MSB first; one row per preset's N):

| N | Presets | Packages |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | `hf_slow`, `hf`, `hf_fast` | 15 packages: `00101101` · `11010100` · `00000000` · `00001001` · `01000011` · `01010001` · `00100000` · `01000100` · `01000101` · `00100000` · `01010000` · `01011001` · `00110010` · `11110100` · `11100101` |
| 16 | `am`, `fm` | 8 packages (the last one short, 8 bits): `0010110111010100` · `0000000000001001` · `0100001101010001` · `0010000001000100` · `0100010100100000` · `0101000001011001` · `0011001011110100` · `11100101` |

### 3.2 "Hi" (the spec's example)

`2D D4 00 02 48 69 93 4A` (CRC 0x934A): with N = 16 the packages `0010110111010100` · `0000000000000010` · `0100100001101001` · `1001001101001010`; with `hf` 98 slots + tail = 13344 samples = 1.668 s.

## 4. Durations (spec 2.4)

`Encoder::duration_samples(n)` = lead + (N_tune + N_sync + B + P + 2)·T·rate + tail samples for n bytes, B = 8n data slots and P = ⌈B/N⌉ STOPs; the last column is what the Encoder rendered.

### 4.1 Segment breakdown

| Preset | Bytes | Lead-in | Tune | Sync | Data slots | STOPs | END | Tail | Slots | `duration_samples` | Rendered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hf` | 2 | 0 ms | 16 | 8 | 16 | 2 | 2 | 100 ms | 44 slots × 16 ms | **6432** (0.804 s) | 6432 |
| `hf_slow` | 15 | 0 ms | 8 | 8 | 120 | 15 | 2 | 100 ms | 153 slots × 32 ms | **39968** (4.996 s) | 39968 |
| `hf` | 15 | 0 ms | 16 | 8 | 120 | 15 | 2 | 100 ms | 161 slots × 16 ms | **21408** (2.676 s) | 21408 |
| `hf_fast` | 15 | 0 ms | 32 | 8 | 120 | 15 | 2 | 100 ms | 177 slots × 8 ms | **12128** (1.516 s) | 12128 |
| `am` | 15 | 0 ms | 32 | 8 | 120 | 8 | 2 | 100 ms | 170 slots × 8 ms | **11680** (1.460 s) | 11680 |
| `fm` | 15 | 300 ms | 63 | 8 | 120 | 8 | 2 | 100 ms | 201 slots × 4 ms | **9632** (1.204 s) | 9632 |

First row: "Hi" (2 bytes, no packet); the others: the 15-byte "CQ DE PY2" packet of section 3.

## 5. Bandwidth (spec 1.5)

### 5.1 Widths per slot length

`occupied_band(tone, T)`: tone ± ⌈4400·500/T_µs⌉ Hz, 99 % of a data slot's energy (4.4/T); `width_26db_hz(T)` = ⌈7000·1000/T_µs⌉ and `width_40db_hz(T)` = ⌈9900·1000/T_µs⌉: outside them a data slot's spectrum stays 26 dB and 40 dB below its centre.

| T | Occupied band (99 %) | At 1500 Hz | −26 dB width | −40 dB width | Presets |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 ms | 1100 Hz | 950–2050 Hz | 1750 Hz | 2475 Hz | `fm` |
| 5 ms | 880 Hz | 1060–1940 Hz | 1400 Hz | 1980 Hz |  |
| 8 ms | 550 Hz | 1225–1775 Hz | 875 Hz | 1238 Hz | `hf_fast`, `am` |
| 12 ms | 368 Hz | 1316–1684 Hz | 584 Hz | 825 Hz |  |
| 16 ms | 276 Hz | 1362–1638 Hz | 438 Hz | 619 Hz | `hf` |
| 20 ms | 220 Hz | 1390–1610 Hz | 350 Hz | 495 Hz |  |
| 32 ms | 138 Hz | 1431–1569 Hz | 219 Hz | 310 Hz | `hf_slow` |
| 64 ms | 70 Hz | 1465–1535 Hz | 110 Hz | 155 Hz |  |
| 128 ms | 36 Hz | 1482–1518 Hz | 55 Hz | 78 Hz |  |

### 5.2 Fit and shift tolerance at 1500 Hz in typical receivers

`passband_fit(config)` of a 1500 Hz sender with slot T in each passband: how far the pitch may move down / up before the band leaves the passband or the pitch leaves the search of the receiver that hears it (300..2700 Hz; from 1000 Hz below 8 ms). ±: the same both ways. Mistuning moves every audio frequency by the same amount; USB tuned too low moves the audio up, LSB the opposite.

| T | SSB 1.8 kHz (300–2100 Hz) | SSB 2.4 kHz (300–2700 Hz) | SSB 2.7 kHz (200–2900 Hz) | SSB 3.0 kHz (100–3000 Hz) | AM (100–3000 Hz) | NBFM (300–3000 Hz) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128 ms | −1182 / +582 | ±1182 | ±1200 | ±1200 | ±1200 | −1182 / +1200 |
| 64 ms | −1165 / +565 | ±1165 | ±1200 | ±1200 | ±1200 | −1165 / +1200 |
| 32 ms | −1131 / +531 | ±1131 | ±1200 | ±1200 | ±1200 | −1131 / +1200 |
| 16 ms | −1062 / +462 | ±1062 | −1162 / +1200 | ±1200 | ±1200 | −1062 / +1200 |
| 8 ms | −925 / +325 | ±925 | −1025 / +1125 | −1125 / +1200 | −1125 / +1200 | −925 / +1200 |
| 4 ms | −500 / +50 | −500 / +650 | −500 / +850 | −500 / +950 | −500 / +950 | −500 / +950 |

### 5.3 The pitch centred in a 1.8 kHz filter

In SSB 1.8 kHz (300–2100 Hz) a pitch of 1200 Hz centres the band: `hf` 1062–1338 Hz, ±762 Hz; `fm` 650–1750 Hz, −200 / +350 Hz (the sender checks it with `EncoderConfig::passband`, `ConfigError::outside_passband`).
